scope: Proposition 5.1 of the manuscript “Finite ordinary minimal model programs on compact Kähler fourfolds” (preprints/Finite-ordinary-minimal-model-programs-on-compact-Kahler-fourfolds-October-6-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 056 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 b1b9511572d6c717), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 22. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let (X, ∆) satisfy the hypotheses of Theorem 1.2. There is an ordinary negative- ray program, finite or infinite, (X, ∆) = (X0, ∆0) 99K (X1, ∆1) 99K · · · , in the same global Weil-divisor Q-factorial compact Kähler category. It stops when the ordinary adjoint is nef or a negative ray has a Mori fibre contraction. Put Di = KXi + ∆i, Li(t) = Di + tHi, Hi = HXi , λ−1 = 1. At every stage before stopping there is a parameter 0 < λi ≤ λi−1 and a contracted extremal ray Ri such that Di · Ri < 0, Li(λi) · Ri = 0, Li(λi) is nef. The generalized pairs (Xi, ∆i + tH) are gklt for 0 ≤ t ≤ λi−1. A birational step is crepant for the data at t = λi, and discrepancies do not decrease across that step for any 0 ≤ t ≤ λi.
